decision: Bartlett Ops Brain repo distribution is strictly local, ever — no public remote.
rationale: Confirmed directly with Mikey when scaffolding the repo. Keeps the secrets/PII bar simple while .gitignore still enforces it as defense-in-depth.
reversalConditions: Mikey explicitly asks to push to a private remote for backup or multi-machine access.

decision: Auto-commit stays OFF by default; every commit is a deliberate, asked-for action.
rationale: Mikey wants to review a run of manual commits before trusting an agent to commit unattended.
reversalConditions: Mikey reviews several manual commits and explicitly asks for auto-commit-on-important-changes.

decision: server/server.js uses only Node's built-in modules (http, fs, path, url, crypto) — no Express, no npm install.
rationale: Matches the existing searchops-helper/server.js pattern already in use for this account, and aligns with the safety rule against running third-party code blindly.
reversalConditions: A concrete feature genuinely requires a dependency Node's stdlib can't reasonably provide.

decision: Cowork access is via the existing 'Copy Cowork brief' read flow plus a paste-back Memory tab, not live remote sync.
rationale: Reconciles 'wire up Cowork access' with 'strictly local, ever' — true remote sync would require a private git remote, out of scope for this pass.
reversalConditions: Mikey wants real-time Cowork read/write against this exact file tree; would require revisiting the local-only decision.

decision: Prioritize disavowing ~319 identified spam backlinks (~140 domains) as the first move to raise Authority Score, ahead of new link-building outreach.
rationale: Authority Score is ~90% a backlink-profile metric and a realistic strong target is ~mid-30s-40s (100 is unreachable for a local business — it's a log-scale metric where national brands sit in the 80s-90s). Cleaning up confirmed toxic links is the more contained first step before investing in new outreach.
reversalConditions: Semrush toxicity data turns out to require manual export with no reliable way to confirm which domains are actually toxic, making the disavow list unreliable to compile safely.

decision: Deploy the Bartlett Ops Brain dashboard live on Railway (private, HTTP Basic Auth-gated, persistent volume) so it's reachable from home, while keeping local http://localhost:4178 available unauthenticated for on-machine work. No GitHub remote was created — deployed via direct `railway up` CLI upload, not a git-linked service.
rationale: Mikey wants to work on this from home, not just this machine. This is the reversal condition explicitly named in dec-local-only ('Mikey explicitly asks to push to a private remote for backup or multi-machine access'), but only partially: the code/data now also lives on Railway's private infrastructure, but never touched a public (or even private) GitHub remote, since gh CLI wasn't available. Basic Auth and a persistent volume were added first since the server had zero authentication and no durable storage across container restarts/redeploys.
reversalConditions: Mikey wants GitHub-linked continuous deployment added (would need gh CLI installed or the repo connected via Railway's dashboard), or wants the live deploy taken down and to go back to local-only.
source: Mikey directly, 2026-07-29 — see memory/log.md (2026-07-29 entry) for the full deploy record.

decision: Standing content-writing rules for all written output: no dashes (em/en dashes or hyphens used as punctuation), write in a human voice, and follow Google's actual content-quality fundamentals rather than trying to defeat AI-detector scores.
rationale: Google's published gen-AI content guidance penalizes low-value, unoriginal, at-scale content, not content because it was AI-assisted. Optimizing to fool an AI-detector targets the wrong signal entirely; optimizing for genuine quality and voice addresses what Google actually penalizes.
reversalConditions: Mikey explicitly asks for a different style rule, or Google's guidance changes in a way that contradicts this framing.
